CO1: Decode a transaction by hand: compute its txid, hash, weight and virtual size from its serialization
CO2: Explain what a full node verifies and why Bitcoin Core's own answers are authoritative
CO3: Choose and justify Bitcoin Core options, such as prune, txindex and dbcache, for a given machine
CO4: Recompute a block's Merkle root and header hash, and check a printed result against the software and the chain
_note: These chapter objectives serve the course outcomes LO-3, LO-6 and LO-7. LO-3, to build, configure and run Bitcoin Core as a full node, to verify the release before trusting it and to query the node over its JSON-RPC interface, is the outcome the whole chapter is written for: its branches are the node, the build, the operation, the interface and the data, which are that outcome's clauses in the chapter's own order, and choosing and justifying options such as pruning, the transaction index and the database cache for a given machine is its configuration half. Decoding a transaction by hand to its identifier, hash, weight and virtual size serves LO-6, on reading transactions and on how a node decides whether one is valid, because those four figures are what the node itself computes from the serialization before it applies any rule. Recomputing a block's Merkle root and header hash, and checking a printed result against the software and against the chain, serves LO-7, on how the chain of blocks and proof of work keep one ledger consistent, since the Merkle root and the header hash are the two commitments that make a block tamper-evident. The ten course outcomes these objectives are aligned to are a DRAFT awaiting the owner's approval: 01-outcomes/sen0401_outcomes_v1_0_0.ttl states, in its own provenance header and in its rdfs:comment, that the outcomes are not approved and that the owner is asked to confirm, revise or reject each one. The alignment below is therefore provisional in the same way, and will be re-stated once the outcomes are ruled on.
